summary: The United States admits Visa Waiver Program nationals with an ESTA travel authorisation ($21, valid 2 years) for stays up to 90 days, lets Canadians visit visa-free for up to 6 months, and requires everyone else to obtain a B1/B2 visitor visa ($185) at a US embassy — often with long interview wait times.

visaTypes.name: ESTA — Electronic System for Travel Authorization

fee.notes: Payable online by card. Covers tourism, business and transit under the Visa Waiver Program; only for nationals of VWP countries.
Non-refundable application (MRV) fee. Requires the DS-160 form and, for most applicants, an in-person interview; appointment wait times vary widely by consulate and can reach several months.

source.name: U.S. Department of State — Visitor Visa

fee.notes: Plus the SEVIS I-901 fee of $350. Requires a Form I-20 from a SEVP-certified school; admitted for 'duration of status' rather than a fixed number of days.

source.name: U.S. Department of State — Student Visa

fee.notes: The US has no airside transit — every passenger clears immigration, so transiting travellers need a C-1 visa unless they hold ESTA or another valid visa. Validity and number of entries depend on the reciprocity schedule for your nationality.

source.name: U.S. Department of State — U.S. Visas

passportValidity.text: As a general rule passports should be valid for 6 months beyond your stay, but nationals of the many countries on the US 'Six-Month Club' exemption list (including all VWP countries) only need a passport valid for the duration of the stay.

source.name: U.S. Customs and Border Protection — International Visitors

travelInsurance.text: Travel insurance is not an entry requirement, but US healthcare is among the most expensive in the world — comprehensive medical cover is essential for any visit.

onwardTicket.text: Travellers entering under the Visa Waiver Program (ESTA) must hold a return or onward ticket; visitor visa holders may also be asked to show one.

proofOfFunds.text: No fixed amount is set, but CBP officers may ask about your funds, accommodation, purpose of visit and ties to home when deciding whether to admit you.

source.name: U.S. Customs and Border Protection — International Visitors

currencyLimits.text: Currency and monetary instruments totalling more than $10,000 must be reported to CBP on arrival and departure (FinCEN Form 105). There is no limit on how much you may carry — only a reporting duty.

source.name: U.S. Customs and Border Protection — Know Before You Go: Money

notes: Visitors may generally bring 1 litre of alcohol and 200 cigarettes duty-free, plus gifts up to about $100 in value.
Agricultural rules are strict — declare all food; fresh fruit, meat and plant products are usually prohibited.

payments.text: Cards and contactless payments are accepted virtually everywhere, and a credit card is expected for hotels and car rental. Tipping is customary — 15–20% in restaurants. Displayed prices usually exclude sales tax.

safety.text: The vast majority of visits are trouble-free. Crime levels vary greatly between cities and neighbourhoods — check local guidance for the areas you visit, and remember that medical treatment is extremely expensive without insurance.

bestTimeToVisit.text: Spring and early autumn suit most regions; the country spans every climate from Alaska to Florida, so the ideal window depends on where you go.

tips.text: Apply for ESTA only at the official site esta.cbp.dhs.gov ($21) — third-party websites charge large mark-ups for the same application.
Submit your ESTA at least 72 hours before departure. Approval is usually quick but is not guaranteed, and airlines will deny boarding without it.
B1/B2 interview appointment wait times at some US consulates run to many months — book your appointment long before planning travel dates.
A simple emergency-room visit can cost thousands of dollars — never travel to the US without medical insurance.

faq.question: What is ESTA and who needs it?
faq.answer: ESTA is the online travel authorisation for the US Visa Waiver Program. Citizens of VWP countries (including the UK, most of Western Europe, Japan, South Korea, Australia and New Zealand) must obtain it before boarding. It costs $21, is valid for 2 years (or until your passport expires) and allows stays of up to 90 days.

faq.question: How long can I stay in the US with ESTA?
faq.answer: Up to 90 days per visit, for tourism, business or transit. The stay cannot be extended, and quick border runs to Canada or Mexico do not reset the 90-day clock.

faq.question: How much does a US visitor visa cost?
faq.answer: The B1/B2 visitor visa application fee is $185. The visa is typically issued as a multiple-entry visa valid up to 10 years for many nationalities, and each admission allows a stay of up to 6 months.

faq.question: Do Canadian citizens need ESTA or a visa for the US?
faq.answer: No. Canadian citizens can enter the United States for tourism or business without a visa or ESTA and stay for up to 6 months.

faq.question: Is Romania in the US Visa Waiver Program?
faq.answer: Romania's VWP designation was announced in early 2025 but was paused before ESTA travel took full effect, so Romanian citizens should assume they need a B1/B2 visa ($185) and check the current status with the US embassy before booking.
